items.title: Somalia braces for El Niño floods as millions face risk of hunger
items.description: In Bayahaaw village, on the outskirts of Jowhar in central Somalia, farmers face a difficult choice: plant crops and risk losing them to floodwaters or leave their fields bare and face potential hunger in the coming year. Nuh Adan, a farmer and community leader in Bayahaaw, said flooding caused by breached riverbanks could devastate local agriculture for months. "If the river breaks and the floods hit us, the effects will last until the next rainy season in March," Adan said. items.description: Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre attended the ceremony, where traditional leaders Ugaas Mohamed Ugaas Kayse and Ugaas Hassan Ugaas Mohamed Ugaas Nuur signed the agreement. items.title: Journalists face arrests and alleged assaults while covering evictions in Somalia and Somaliland
items.description: The Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) says it has documented 13 arbitrary arrests of journalists in Mogadishu since Jan. 1, 2026, while 10 journalists have been arrested in Somaliland during the same period. items.description: The boat went down during the night of Oct. 8-9 near Guehere, north of the port town of Obock. The death toll rose from 109 after 30 more bodies were recovered, the International Organization for Migration said. About 82 people survived, while search and recovery operations continued. The shipwreck is among the deadliest recorded on the Eastern Route, a migration corridor used by people traveling from the Horn of Africa toward Yemen and other destinations in the Arabian Peninsula.
